is_anopheles.evidence: The study is a theoretical mathematical modelling paper focusing primarily on arboviral disease vectors (Aedes aegypti), with Anopheles mentioned only as background/literature discussion (e.g. pages 2, 11).

reports_target_markers.evidence: No empirical genotyping of any insecticide resistance target markers was performed; the paper uses abstract alleles (A and a) in ordinary differential equation simulations.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No real mosquito genotype or allele count data are reported; all frequencies and numbers represent simulated model parameters.

african_field_population.evidence: No field-collected mosquitoes were sampled or tested.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a theoretical mathematical modelling and numerical simulation study, not an empirical primary study of mosquito populations.

sub_country_location.evidence: No sampling sites exist as no field specimens were collected.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: No collection dates exist as no field mosquitoes were collected.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary data needed; study is fundamentally ineligible.

assessment.summary: This article describes a deterministic compartmental mathematical model (SIRSI) incorporating vector population genetics (dominant and recessive resistance alleles) to simulate vector-borne arboviral epidemics. It does not collect or genotype real Anopheles mosquitoes.
